annotations.text:
WORKBENCH — chosen.

The bet: it is a power tool with 200 endpoints, so stop apologising for that. Hierarchy comes from structure — panes, tabs, tables, a status bar — instead of from 31 identically-weighted labels.

Same tokens as before. Nothing here is a new colour.

A turn is SELECTED (j/k), which is what gives ⌘K something to act on. Its four common actions sit in place with their keys; the other fifteen are two keystrokes away. The status bar collects every chip that used to float on some other screen.

The 19-button sheet AND the ops grid, replaced by one thing. Scoped to the selected turn — the header says which — and grouped: this turn, this roleplay, go to. Fuzzy match, so "dr" finds Draw this and Director note.

31 section labels in one 1,596-line scroll become 8 categories and a filter. Rows are a table with columns that mean something; editing opens IN the pane rather than in a stack of sheets. Sign out finally exists.

The direction's real test, since it is desktop-shaped. Three panes collapse to one: the rail becomes the back arrow, the inspector becomes the status bar, and the palette gives the phone all 200 commands without a single stacked-button sheet.
Kept for the record. Manuscript's margin idea and Room's presence strip are both liftable into Workbench later if wanted — they are not mutually exclusive with it.
